rationale:
Evidence: iteration 5 (score 851, best so far) is the only design with every development track finishing at least half the time. Oval (20/20) and s-bend (20/20) are solid. Slalom is the gap: 11/20 finish, 7 off-track exits, 2 timeouts, mean progress 0.90, max_error 0.042, and 0.5 line-loss events. The timeouts and a mean finish time of 2.92 s show the slalom is also near the speed limit. Iteration 4 showed that raising kp to 6 collapses the oval and s-bend, so kp stays at 4.0. Body width cannot widen the off-track limit because the 0.06 m floor binds, so it stays at 0.12. The 2 percent disturbance is the same for every design, so the comparison stays fair.

Changes from iteration 5: (1) Reduce mass from 0.45 to 0.40 kg, the lower bound. Iteration 3 to 5 showed that lower mass cut slalom max_error and line loss while the oval and s-bend improved. Lower yaw inertia should help the sharp slalom direction changes, and the faster acceleration should help the timeouts. (2) Move all five sensors forward from y = 0.05 to y = 0.06 m. This gives the steering a little more lead, which the Evaluator suggested as the next lever after the mass change. Sensor x positions, the 16 mm size, the weights [-2,-1,0,1,2], kd 1.0, ki 0.05, base_speed 1.5, and line_loss last_direction are unchanged, so the effect of these two changes is easier to read.

Expected result: slalom off-track exits fall below 5 of 20, slalom finishes rise above 11 of 20, and slalom max_error stays near or below 0.042. Oval and s-bend completion should hold near 100 percent. Hypotheses: (a) mass 0.40 reduces slalom max_error and line-loss events further; (b) the sensor lead at y = 0.06 reduces slalom off-track exits without adding oscillation above about 0.35; (c) the timeouts disappear because the lighter robot reaches speed sooner. Measurements wanted next: per-track completion, max_error, line_loss_events and completion_time on slalom, plus steering_oscillation on all tracks, so I can tell whether the sensor lead or the mass change drives any gain. If slalom still leaves the track, the next step is a small kd increase, not kp.
